title: Alleged B.C. gunman shot by police
article: Police shot and killed a man considered a person of interest in Sunday's double homicide at a sushi house in nearby Burnaby who was also suspected of shooting his former landlord on Tuesday.
Angus David Mitchell, 26, was taken to hospital in "grave" condition Wednesday afternoon following a standoff with police in Maple Ridge, B.C. He was later pronounced dead in hospital.
Earlier in the day, Burnaby RCMP issued a warning to the public that Mitchell was armed with a scoped hunting rifle.
RCMP Insp. Tim Shields said Mitchell, a former security guard, appeared to be unpredictable and emotionally unstable prior to the police standoff.

He said Mitchell was evicted from a residence in Vancouver about six months ago. He allegedly went to his former landlord's Burnaby home Tuesday and shot him. The 51-year-old man was severely injured.
Shields said Mitchell had prior conflicts with both the landlord and his former employer.
He confirmed Mitchell legally purchased a scoped hunting rifle within the past six months and has also come up on "police radar" during that same period. He was never charged with a crime.
Sgt. Jennifer Pound confirmed Mitchell was also a person of interest in Sunday's double homicide at Royal Oak Sushi House.
She said police believe the cases are connected because of the severity of what occurred and geographic proximity of both crimes.

On a Facebook page of a man identified as Angus Mitchell - with the same pictures the RCMP released - the poster suggests he has a grudge against the president of Victoria-based Themis Security Services.

"Every time I had dealt with you I have showed you patience and regard as the 'president' of the company and look at what you do..?" the post says. "You (expletive) up your own payroll so I cannot get paid on time...don't you ever try and talk to me as if you can give me an order."
